title: Horrible
subtitle: 「可怕的／糟糕的／令人不快的」，究竟是哪一種 horrible？
description: 「可怕的／糟糕的／令人不快的」，究竟是哪一種 horrible？

words.note: 最常見、最靈活的強烈近義詞之一，可形容經驗、天氣、味道、表現、感受等。
words.example: We had awful weather throughout the trip.
words.exampleZh: 整趟旅程的天氣都糟透了。

exercises.original: We had horrible weather for the entire weekend.
exercises.zh: 整個週末天氣都糟透了。
exercises.upgrade: awful · 糟糕的；可怕的；很差的

options.explanation: awful weather 是非常常見的日常搭配，表示天氣非常差。這裡沒有恐怖、噁心或道德震驚等更窄意味，因此 awful 最自然。
hideous 主要形容外觀醜陋；雖偶可誇張使用，但不如 awful 自然描述一般壞天氣。
通常用於嚴重事故、暴力、創傷等駭人事件；普通壞天氣力度和語義都不合。
可形容天氣陰沉，但更常指前景、現實或情勢嚴峻；這裡只是一般「天氣很糟」。
強調噁心、令人作嘔，不自然形容天氣。
描述人的感受，不能修飾 weather。

exercises.original: The restaurant gave us horrible service from start to finish.
exercises.zh: 餐廳由頭到尾的服務都糟透了。

options.explanation: awful service 是標準日常搭配，單純表示服務品質非常差。
對一般服務品質過強，通常帶創傷／恐怖意味。
偏外觀醜陋，不形容服務品質。
偏噁心或令人厭惡，不是一般服務差。
可描述情勢、前景，但不常搭 service。

exercises.original: I had a horrible headache all afternoon.
exercises.zh: 我整個下午都頭痛得很厲害。

options.explanation: awful headache 是自然常見搭配，表示疼痛感很嚴重、令人難受。
通常指外觀醜陋，不自然描述普通頭痛。
多形容前景、現實、消息或嚴峻情勢。
是「令人作嘔」，不合疼痛程度。
通常帶震驚／譴責感，不是 headache 的自然首選。
名詞，不能直接修飾 headache。

words.note: 力度比 horrible 弱，較中性正式，強調不舒服、不愉快，而未必「非常糟糕」。
words.example: The room had an unpleasant smell.
words.exampleZh: 房間裡有一股令人不快的氣味。

exercises.original: The medicine left a horrible taste in my mouth, but it was not unbearable.
exercises.zh: 這藥在我口中留下令人不快的味道，但還不至於難以忍受。
exercises.upgrade: unpleasant · 令人不快的；不舒服的

options.explanation: not unbearable 是關鍵線索，表示不舒服但程度有限；unpleasant taste 精確而不誇張。
力度過強，通常表示極其糟糕。
帶恐怖／創傷意味，完全不合味覺。
可形容極差味道，但比原句語氣強。
可口語誇張形容味道，但主要偏外觀且較強烈。
副詞，不能修飾名詞 taste。

exercises.original: The meeting became horrible when the discussion turned tense, though nobody shouted.
exercises.zh: 討論變得緊張後，會議變得令人不愉快，但沒有人大叫。

options.explanation: tension + nobody shouted 表示氣氛不舒服但未到極端，unpleasant 的強度最合適。
極差或令人髮指，與輕度緊張會議不成比例。
帶震驚／難以接受意味，也太強。
更戲劇化，通常不如 unpleasant 精準。

exercises.original: There was a horrible smell in the corridor, but it faded after a few minutes.
exercises.zh: 走廊有一股令人不快的氣味，但幾分鐘後就散了。

options.explanation: 一般令人不舒服的 smell 最自然用 unpleasant；原句也沒有說噁心得令人作嘔。
可誇張，但通常比情境需要的強。
力度過強且較偏品質評價。

words.note: 英式英語尤其常見，可表示非常差、非常令人不快，也可帶可怕意味。
words.example: The service at the hotel was dreadful.

exercises.original: The hotel breakfast was horrible, and almost everything was cold.
exercises.zh: 酒店早餐糟透了，幾乎所有食物都是冷的。
exercises.upgrade: dreadful · 糟透的；可怕的；極差的

options.explanation: British English 中 dreadful 很自然形容食物／服務整體品質極差；冷掉的早餐正符合此類日常抱怨。
更常描述前景、現實或陰沉情勢，不是早餐品質。
若味道噁心得令人作嘔可以用，但原句重點只是品質差、食物冷。
副詞，was 後需要形容詞。

exercises.original: We had a horrible journey because the train was delayed for six hours.
exercises.zh: 火車延誤六小時，我們的旅程糟透了。

options.explanation: dreadful journey 是自然英式搭配，表示整段經歷非常差。
通常意味更嚴重創傷性事件。
可形容旅程情勢嚴峻，但不如 dreadful 日常自然。

exercises.original: His first attempt at the speech was horrible, but he improved after practising.
exercises.zh: 他第一次演講表現糟透了，但練習後有所改善。

options.explanation: performance quality is the issue; dreadful naturally means extremely poor.
not a natural evaluation of a speech performance.

words.note: 非常常見，既可形容品質差，也可形容嚴重事件、疼痛、錯誤或情況。
words.exampleZh: 他犯了一個嚴重的錯誤。

exercises.original: He made a horrible mistake that cost the company a large amount of money.
exercises.zh: 他犯了一個嚴重錯誤，令公司損失大量金錢。
exercises.upgrade: terrible · 很糟的；可怕的；嚴重的

options.explanation: terrible mistake 是高頻搭配，並且大額損失提供「嚴重」線索。
只表示令人不快，力度不足以表達重大錯誤後果。

exercises.original: She was in horrible pain after the accident.
exercises.zh: 事故後她痛得很厲害。

options.explanation: 固定高頻搭配 terrible pain 表示強烈疼痛。
通常不用來中性描述痛楚程度。
不搭 pain 作一般強度描述。
表示噁心，不是疼痛程度。
名詞，表示恐怖，不是 pain 的形容詞。

exercises.original: The team had a horrible season and won only two matches.
exercises.zh: 球隊這一季表現很糟，只贏了兩場。

options.explanation: terrible season 是自然的整體表現評價，兩勝提供成績很差的依據。
對運動賽季過度帶恐怖意味。
副詞，不能直接修飾 season。
表示受到恐嚇／恐怖侵擾，意思不同。

words.meaning: 駭人的；令人震驚地糟糕的
words.note: 表示某事差到令人震驚、憤怒或難以接受，常用於行為、條件、服務、統計或事件。
words.example: The workers were living in appalling conditions.
words.exampleZh: 工人生活在令人震驚的惡劣環境中。

exercises.original: Investigators found that workers were living in horrible conditions without clean water.
exercises.zh: 調查人員發現工人生活環境惡劣得令人震驚，甚至沒有乾淨食水。
exercises.upgrade: appalling · 駭人的；令人震驚地糟糕的

options.explanation: without clean water + investigators 表示條件差到令人震驚、難以接受；appalling conditions 是典型搭配。
力度太弱，無法反映基本生活條件嚴重不足。
偏外觀醜陋，不是生活條件的主要評價。
描述人感到震驚，例如 investigators were appalled；不能修飾 conditions。

exercises.original: The report described horrible treatment of vulnerable patients.
exercises.zh: 報告描述弱勢病人受到令人震驚的惡劣對待。
exercises.upgrade: appalling · 令人震驚地惡劣的

options.explanation: treatment of vulnerable patients in a report invites moral disapproval and shock; appalling treatment is highly idiomatic.
appearance-focused and grammatically changes the meaning.

exercises.original: The service was horrible: customers waited three hours and nobody explained the delay.
exercises.zh: 服務差得令人震驚：顧客等了三小時，而且沒有人解釋延誤。
exercises.upgrade: appalling · 糟糕得令人震驚的

options.explanation: three-hour wait + no explanation justifies an emphatic judgement of service as shockingly bad.
wrong noun phrase and semantic domain.
adverb; after was use adjective appalling.

words.note: 強烈程度很高，可形容事故、經歷、費用、交通、傷勢等，語氣比 ordinary bad 強很多。
words.example: We were stuck in horrendous traffic.
words.exampleZh: 我們困在極其糟糕的交通中。

exercises.original: We were caught in horrible traffic and moved only two kilometres in an hour.
exercises.zh: 我們遇上極其糟糕的交通，一小時只走了兩公里。
exercises.upgrade: horrendous · 極其可怕的；極糟的

options.explanation: horrendous traffic 是常見強烈搭配，一小時只走兩公里支持極端程度。
可說 traffic situation was grim，但不如 horrendous traffic 直接自然。

exercises.original: The project suffered horrible delays after the supplier failed to deliver key parts.
exercises.zh: 供應商未能交付關鍵零件後，項目出現極其嚴重的延誤。

options.explanation: major project delays caused by missing key parts justify a very strong adjective; horrendous delays is natural.

exercises.original: She had a horrible experience trying to get home during the storm.
exercises.zh: 暴風雨期間，她回家的經歷極其糟糕。

options.explanation: storm + difficult journey supports an emphatic description of the overall experience.

words.meaning: 可怕的；令人不舒服的；糟透的
words.note: 較英式、較生動，可形容外觀、味道、顏色、經驗或情況令人難受。
words.example: The walls were painted a ghastly shade of green.
words.exampleZh: 牆壁被漆成一種難看得要命的綠色。

exercises.original: The room had horrible green wallpaper that made the whole place look sickly.
exercises.zh: 房間的綠色牆紙難看得要命，令整個地方看起來病懨懨。
exercises.upgrade: ghastly · 可怕的；令人不舒服的；糟透的

options.explanation: colour/appearance + strong dislike is a very natural British-style use of ghastly.
more about bleak situations than ugly wallpaper.

exercises.original: The soup had a horrible grey colour and tasted just as bad.
exercises.zh: 湯呈現難看的灰色，味道也同樣糟。

options.explanation: unappealing colour + bad taste suits the vivid, disgusted tone of ghastly.
not normally used for food colour.

exercises.original: We spent a horrible evening in a freezing room with no electricity.
exercises.zh: 我們在沒有電、冷得要命的房間裡度過了一個非常難受的晚上。

options.explanation: freezing room with no electricity makes the whole evening deeply unpleasant; ghastly is vivid but natural.
too strongly linked to trauma or violence.
standard noun would be ghastliness; here an adjective is needed anyway.

words.note: 常表示品質、表現、天氣、服務極差，也可形容道德上令人髮指的行為。

exercises.original: The road conditions were horrible after days of heavy rain.
exercises.zh: 連日大雨後，路況惡劣至極。
exercises.upgrade: atrocious · 惡劣的；糟糕透頂的

options.explanation: atrocious conditions 是自然強烈搭配，特別適合極差路況。
外觀導向，不是道路可用性／品質。
名詞，表示暴行／極惡劣之事。

exercises.original: His performance was horrible: he missed almost every easy shot.
exercises.zh: 他的表現糟糕透頂，幾乎每個簡單射門都失手。

options.explanation: performance + repeated obvious failures is a classic context for atrocious performance.
too weak and does not naturally rate performance quality.
can describe prospects or scenes, not usually a sports performance.

exercises.original: Residents complained about the horrible state of the public toilets.
exercises.zh: 居民投訴公共廁所狀況極其惡劣。

options.explanation: atrocious state/condition strongly expresses unacceptable poor quality or maintenance.

words.meaning: 醜陋可怕的；令人厭惡的
words.note: 特別常形容外觀、顏色、服裝、設計很醜，也可較文學地形容令人恐懼或厭惡的東西。
words.example: They replaced the hideous old carpet.
words.exampleZh: 他們換掉了那張難看得要命的舊地毯。

exercises.original: They removed the horrible patterned carpet because everyone thought it was ugly.
exercises.zh: 大家都覺得那張有花紋的地毯難看，所以把它拆掉。
exercises.upgrade: hideous · 醜陋可怕的；令人厭惡的

options.explanation: everyone thought it was ugly directly identifies appearance as the problem; hideous is the strongest precise visual adjective here.
not an appearance word in this sense.
could express strong disapproval, but less specifically visual than hideous.

exercises.original: She refused to wear the horrible orange jacket because she hated its appearance.
exercises.zh: 她拒絕穿那件難看的橙色外套，因為她討厭它的外觀。

options.explanation: clothing + appearance dislike is a prototypical hideous context.

exercises.original: The redesign produced a horrible logo with clashing colours and awkward lettering.
exercises.zh: 重新設計後的標誌顏色衝突、字體彆扭，醜得可怕。

options.explanation: clashing colours + awkward lettering are explicitly visual defects, making hideous the precise synonym.

words.meaning: 令人不快的；討厭的；惡劣的
words.note: 口語常見，可形容味道、傷口、天氣、驚喜、事故或人的態度，通常比 horrible 稍口語。
words.example: He received a nasty cut on his hand.
words.exampleZh: 他的手割了一道很嚴重的傷口。

exercises.original: He got a horrible cut on his hand while opening the box.
exercises.zh: 他開箱時手被割了一道很嚴重的傷口。
exercises.upgrade: nasty · 令人不快的；惡劣的

options.explanation: nasty cut 是高頻口語搭配，表示傷口不輕、令人不舒服。
可能形容傷口外觀非常可怕，但普通受傷敘述中不如 nasty 自然。
強調令人作嘔，除非特別描寫外觀。

exercises.original: We had a horrible surprise when the repair bill arrived.
exercises.zh: 維修帳單送來時，我們遇到了一個很討厭的意外驚喜。

options.explanation: 固定搭配 a nasty surprise 表示令人不快、意料之外的壞消息或情況。

exercises.original: The cyclist had a horrible fall on the wet road but avoided serious injury.
exercises.zh: 單車手在濕路上狠狠摔了一跤，但沒有嚴重受傷。

options.explanation: a nasty fall 是自然口語搭配，表示跌得不輕，但後文又說沒有 serious injury，因此不需用 horrific。
把普通事故誇張成災難，而且詞性／受詞都改變。

words.meaning: 令人作嘔的；噁心的；令人厭惡的
words.note: 強調強烈厭惡，特別適合味道、氣味、食物、骯髒狀況或令人反感的行為。

exercises.original: The food smelled horrible after being left in the heat all day.
exercises.zh: 食物在高溫中放了一整天後，聞起來令人作嘔。
exercises.upgrade: revolting · 令人作嘔的；噁心的；令人厭惡的

options.explanation: spoiled food + smell is a prototypical disgust context; revolting directly means strongly disgusting.
can be informal but is primarily visual.
describes a person's reaction: I was revolted.

exercises.original: The drain gave off a horrible smell that made everyone step back.
exercises.zh: 排水渠散發出令人噁心的氣味，令所有人退後。

options.explanation: strong smell causing a physical disgust reaction is exactly the semantic territory of revolting.

exercises.original: Everyone found the man's horrible table manners disgusting.
exercises.zh: 大家都覺得那名男子的餐桌禮儀令人厭惡。

options.explanation: disgusting is essentially the decisive semantic clue; behaviour can be revolting when it provokes strong disgust.
not a disgust adjective for manners.
describes the people: everyone was revolted; the manners themselves are revolting.

words.meaning: 駭人的；恐怖的；令人震驚的
words.note: 通常用於嚴重事故、暴力、傷害、災難或創傷性事件，帶明顯恐怖與震驚感。
words.exampleZh: 報告描述了駭人的傷勢。

exercises.original: The crash caused horrible injuries to several passengers.
exercises.zh: 撞車事故令數名乘客遭受駭人的傷勢。
exercises.upgrade: horrific · 駭人的；恐怖的；令人震驚的

options.explanation: serious crash + severe injuries is a classic trauma context for horrific injuries.
could describe appearance, but does not primarily encode traumatic severity.
nasty injuries can be natural, but horrific better matches a severe crash with multiple passengers.

exercises.original: Witnesses described the horrible scene after the explosion.
exercises.zh: 目擊者形容爆炸後的場面十分駭人。

options.explanation: explosion aftermath + witness accounts supports genuine horror/shock, not merely poor quality.
appearance may be part of it, but horrific captures the traumatic event more fully.

exercises.original: The documentary contains horrible accounts of violence during the conflict.
exercises.zh: 紀錄片包含衝突期間駭人的暴力描述。

options.explanation: violence during conflict is a strong trauma/horror context, exactly where horrific is natural.
can express ugliness/repulsiveness but is less precise for violent accounts.

words.meaning: 嚴峻的；陰沉可怕的；令人沮喪的
words.note: 表示情況非常不樂觀、殘酷或令人沮喪，常用於前景、現實、消息、條件。

exercises.original: The economic future looks horrible if unemployment continues to rise.
exercises.zh: 如果失業率持續上升，經濟前景看來十分嚴峻。
exercises.upgrade: grim · 嚴峻的；令人沮喪的

options.explanation: economic outlook + rising unemployment is a standard bleak/serious forecast context for grim.
visual phrasing does not suit an economic outlook.
adverb; looks takes adjective complement grim.

exercises.original: The report gives a horrible picture of living conditions in the region.
exercises.zh: 報告描繪該區生活條件十分嚴峻。

options.explanation: fixed collocation a grim picture means a bleak, serious account of a difficult reality.
would emphasize disgust rather than bleakness.
visual ugliness is not the main point.

exercises.original: The doctors gave the family horrible news about the patient's chances of recovery.
exercises.zh: 醫生向家屬傳達了關於病人康復機會的令人沮喪消息。

options.explanation: poor prognosis + serious news strongly supports grim news, meaning bleak and discouraging.

words.meaning: 令人難受的；糟糕的；悲慘的
words.note: 可表示某段經歷令人非常不舒服、不開心，或某人處於痛苦、悲慘狀態。
words.example: We spent a miserable night in the cold.
words.exampleZh: 我們在寒冷中度過了難熬的一夜。

exercises.original: We spent a horrible night in a cold tent while rain leaked through the roof.
exercises.zh: 我們在寒冷帳篷裡度過了難熬的一夜，雨水還從帳篷頂漏進來。
exercises.upgrade: miserable · 令人難受的；糟糕的；悲慘的

options.explanation: cold + leaking rain creates sustained discomfort and unhappiness, a prototypical miserable night.
too trauma-focused unless something truly horrifying happened.

exercises.original: The children had a horrible afternoon stuck indoors with no heating.
exercises.zh: 孩子們沒有暖氣又被困在室內，度過了一個很難受的下午。

options.explanation: the sentence focuses on prolonged discomfort and unhappiness, not horror or disgust.

exercises.original: He had a horrible journey home, feeling cold, tired, and sick the whole way.
exercises.zh: 他回家的旅程非常難受，一路上又冷、又累、又不舒服。

options.explanation: cold + tired + sick describes personal discomfort and unhappiness throughout the experience.
strong disgust, not the main emotion.

falseSynonyms.zh: 兩者都可表示「糟透了」，但 awful 在日常英語中特別廣泛。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The hotel was horrible. The service was awful.

falseSynonyms.zh: unpleasant 不一定達到 horrible 的強烈程度。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The conversation was unpleasant. The accident scene was horrible.

falseSynonyms.zh: 普通的糟糕服務通常不能自然叫 horrific。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The service was horrible. The crash caused horrific injuries.

falseSynonyms.zh: 它不是一般 bad experience 的自由替代。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON We had a horrible journey. The room had hideous wallpaper.

falseSynonyms.zh: 若只是服務差，不一定叫 revolting。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The service was horrible. The smell from the bin was revolting.

falseSynonyms.zh: 它常用於 outlook、reality、conditions，而不是味道或顏色。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The food tasted horrible. The economic outlook is grim.

falseSynonyms.zh: nasty 不一定像 horrible 一樣強烈，但在傷口、意外、氣味等語境很自然。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON She had a nasty fall. It was a horrible experience overall.

falseSynonyms.zh: horrible 描述事物令人害怕／糟糕；horrified 描述人感到震驚或恐懼。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON It was a horrible sight. She was horrified by what she saw.
